correctness.rationale: Taking \(r=x/y\) cancels the cubic terms to \(\dot r=y^2(1-r^2)\). The scalar solution \(y^2=b^2e^{2t}/[1-pb^2(e^{2t}-1)]\) defines a strictly increasing internal clock \(I=\int_0^t y^2\). The exact ratio trajectory \(r=(1+Ke^{-2I})/(1-Ke^{-2I})\) has its only pole at \(I=\frac12\log K\), before any scalar blow-up, giving the physical-time formula and \(x(t)\sim-1/[Y(T_p-t)]\) with finite \(Y>0\). Expansion of the exact time formula gives the three regimes; for \(p>0\), the exact difference \(t_b-T_p=-\frac12\log[1-K^{-p}/(1+pb^2)]\) has leading coefficient \(2^{-p-1}/(1+pb^2)\) and noninteger Hölder order \(p\). Setting \(p=\delta/\log K\) gives an exact \(F(\delta)=(1-e^{-\delta})/\delta\) crossover and compact-\(\delta\) uniform error. On the invariant line \(x=-y\) the positive-p blow-up exponent is \(1/2\), whereas on the escape side it is one. The actual check.py was read and checks these cancellations and sample limits numerically; no finite computation is used to prove the asymptotic quantifiers.

value.rationale: Exact separatrix residence-time scaling in a canonical integrable cubic flow is motivated by global phase portrait theory. The three-regime transition, sharp Hölder exponent and uniform two-parameter crossover give nontrivial quantitative information beyond qualitative orbit classification.

final_claim: For the cubic Darboux flow \(\dot x=x-x^2y+pxy^2+y^3\), \(\dot y=y+py^3\) and initial data \((x_0,y_0)=(-(1+\varepsilon)b,b)\), \(b,\varepsilon>0\), the first finite physical-time escape is \(T_p=\frac12\log[1+(1-K^{-p})/(pb^2)]\) for \(p\ne0\), \(T_0=\frac12\log[1+(\log K)/b^2]\), \(K=(2+\varepsilon)/\varepsilon\). The approach to the invariant line shows logarithmic \(p<0\), double-logarithmic \(p=0\), and Hölder/analytic \(p>0\) clock limits, with uniform crossover under \(p=\delta/\log K\), and distinct on/off separatrix blow-up exponents.
limitations: Only the specified integrable real cubic Darboux system and escape-side initial data; no generic perturbation theorem or uniform estimate for unbounded crossover parameter.
Original 2023 source and older related papers were not available in fully verified primary text, creating an originality residual risk.
